speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To understand the cause of these symptoms, could you tell me how long you've been experiencing these issues and whether they are getting worse?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fact that your double vision occurs with upward or downward gaze, and your weakness worsens with activity but improves with rest, is highly suggestive of a neuromuscular issue. To confirm this, I need to know if you experience any drooping eyelids (ptosis) and if you have difficulty swallowing or speaking. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.

The presence of elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies, combined with your fluctuating weakness, diplopia on vertical gaze, and absence of sensory deficits, confirms this autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder. Do you have a history of thymoma or any prior chest imaging to evaluate your thymus gland?
